stem: A client with asthma asks which exposures can trigger symptoms. Which response is accurate?

options.A: Exercise is the only predictable asthma trigger, so viral infections, smoke, cold air, and allergens do not need consideration.
options.B: Asthma triggers may include respiratory infections, poor air quality or smoke, very cold air, physical activity, and relevant indoor or outdoor allergens, with individual variation.
options.C: Environmental triggers stop influencing asthma after controller therapy is prescribed, making exposure assessment unnecessary.
options.D: Asthma exacerbations occur independently of recognizable exposures, so identifying individual triggers does not help management.

rationale: NHLBI lists indoor and outdoor allergens, physical activity, respiratory infections, poor air quality, and very cold air among common asthma triggers. Trigger patterns vary among individuals, and identifying/avoiding relevant triggers is part of asthma management. B is correct.
educational_objective: Teach that asthma symptoms can be triggered by infections, allergens, exercise, cold air, smoke/poor air quality, and other individual exposures.
source_organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), NIH
source_locator: Asthma triggers: indoor/outdoor allergens, physical activity, infections such as colds/flu/COVID-19, poor air quality, and very cold air; managing asthma includes identifying and avoiding relevant triggers.
source_claim_supported: Asthma symptoms can be triggered by respiratory infections, allergens, physical activity, poor air quality/smoke-related exposures, and cold air, with patterns varying by individual.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: provide care for acute/chronic conditions, recognize contributing pathophysiologic factors and complications, and provide appropriate interventions/education.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — asthma triggers and chronic respiratory management

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because multiple common triggers beyond exercise are documented.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because controller therapy does not eliminate the relevance of exposure triggers.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because identifying and avoiding triggers is part of asthma management.
